title: The CPU Press
topic: Loops: while, for, range, break and continue
briefing: Sorting one chip at a time is too slow. The CPU press can stamp out chips all day, as long as someone keeps pressing the button. That someone is a loop! Keep it running while it has power, skip dead chips, and if a chip comes out dangerously hot, STOP THE PRESS immediately.
hints: while press.has_power(): keeps looping as long as there's power. Inside the loop, cpu = press.stamp() makes a chip.

Inside the loop, check the overheating chip first: if cpu["temp_c"] > 100, then print a warning and break. For a dead chip (clock_ghz == 0), add 1 to dead and continue. Otherwise append the chip to good.

Countdown: for i in range(3, 0, -1): print(i). Loop: while press.has_power(): cpu = press.stamp() / if cpu["temp_c"] > 100: break / if cpu["clock_ghz"] == 0: dead += 1; continue / good.append(cpu). Afterwards: for cpu in good: print(cpu["serial"])
bonus: Use a nested loop to print a 3x3 grid of chip slots like A1 A2 A3 / B1 B2 B3 / C1 C2 C3.
